title: When the Guard Adds Nothing: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for LLM‑Produced Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to measure whether a deterministic generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline increases the probability that an LLM‑produced vendor CLI configuration passes a conservative deterministic validator, relative to direct LLM generation. The preregistered protocol froze a single shared initial candidate per task (one generator call shared by both arms) and allowed at most one automatic repair call for the guarded arm if the shared initial failed. Using a curated 300‑task multi‑vendor manifest and the declared generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa), every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: baseline = 300/300; guarded = 300/300 (paired table n11=300, n10=n01=n00=0). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Because no initial failures occurred, the preregistered single‑repair policy was never invoked. We release the full preregistration, task manifest, raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with canonical SHA‑256 hashes to enable exact reproduction and controlled follow‑ups.

sections.introduction: LLM‑based intent→configuration systems promise faster NetOps workflows but raise operational safety concerns: generated CLI fragments must respect syntactic, resource, and workflow invariants before application. A commonly proposed architectural safeguard is generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R): a generator proposes a candidate, a deterministic validator checks conservative invariants, and a bounded repair step attempts a model‑guided correction when the validator fails. Prior work has advocated verifier‑anchored self‑correction and tool‑assisted refinement, but evidence quantifying the marginal operational benefit of a bounded repair stage—holding generator snapshot, prompt, and validator fixed—is limited. We preregistered a paired design that shares each task's initial generator output between baseline and guarded arms to isolate the marginal effect of a single automatic repair call. The preregistration, the manifest, the validator, all prompts, and execution artifacts were frozen and archived prior to model calls (see preregistration and execution manifest hashes in the Disclosure). Our core research question: under the frozen shared‑initial design, does permitting exactly one automatic repair call increase the per‑task probability of producing a deterministic‑validator‑passing configuration?
sections.related_work: Intent‑driven configuration and LLM‑assisted NetOps have rapidly advanced (see Nguyen et al., 2024 for formal intent translation with LLMs; Chakraborty et al., CNSM 2024 for LLM configuration generation demos). Tool‑augmented self‑refinement and bounded self‑correction architectures (e.g., INTERACSPARQL style pipelines and other RAG/self‑refine works) motivated our bounded repair policy. Formal verification and SMT‑based policy checking for BGP/ISP policies informed our conservative validator design (e.g., Bagpipe / Weitz et al., 2016). Unlike broad model leaderboards, our study isolates an operational question—marginal value of a single bounded repair call—under a frozen generator, prompt, and validator so conclusions about repair utility are directly actionable for pipeline architects.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a machine‑readable experimental plan (study_hosted_netops_gvr_v1_cnd_7a3f2b1e; preregistration SHA‑256 = a85d66d4c6ce2275e2d8c820f96c610532dbb5452bebb3fe108848f9dc38cdf6). Design: paired tasks (n=300). For each task a single shared initial candidate was produced by the declared generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Baseline outcome = validator(initial). Guarded outcome = validator(initial) OR (if initial failed) a single automatic repair call and revalidation. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Stopping, retry, missingness, and multiplicity plans were fixed in the preregistration and archived.
sections.results: Execution accounting and primary outcome. The run executed exactly as preregistered under adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × shared initial), completed = 600, failed episodes = 0, model calls used = 300 (one shared initial generation per task). Repair calls were permitted by design but never invoked (repair_call_count = 0). Every shared initial candidate passed the conservative deterministic validator: baseline_success_count = 300/300; guarded_success_count = 300/300. The paired contingency table is n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The analysis artifact bundle (analysis/*) and the full execution manifest enumerate and hash every raw response, provider trace, and validator trace used to compute these numbers (execution/execution_manifest.json lists all paths and SHA‑256 values). Representative per‑episode scoring artifacts are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = 1c3cbbeb30cb9d03...).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. Under the frozen shared‑initial design and the declared generator snapshot, the generator produced validator‑compliant outputs for every task in the curated 300‑task manifest. Consequently a bounded single automatic repair could not improve the deterministic pass rate because there were no initial failures to repair. The observed ceiling (zero discordant pairs) is a valid experimental outcome; it means that in this specific regime adding an automated single‑attempt repair stage would have increased computational and operational cost without increasing deterministic validator pass probability.

Per‑vendor preregistered secondary tests. The protocol preregistered per‑vendor paired comparisons as secondary estimands. Because the observed global contingency table contains zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0), every per‑vendor contingency table—being a partition of the same paired outcomes—also contains zero discordant pairs and the per‑vendor McNemar tests are therefore non‑informative. The canonical task manifest (artifact: execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3) is the artifact we would use to compute per‑vendor counts; auditors can replay the manifest against archived responses to recompute vendor‑level tables if they wish. We explicitly report that the preregistered per‑vendor tests were executed as planned but produced no discordance because all shared initial candidates passed the validator, so no repair‑effect signal could be measured by those tests.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment asking whether permitting a single bounded automatic repair increases deterministic‑validator pass probability over direct generation when the same initial candidate is shared between arms. Under the frozen generator snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini), prompt family, and the curated 300‑task manifest, every shared initial candidate passed our conservative deterministic validator. The paired outcome is therefore exactly null: paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. Importantly, this null is artifact‑grounded and reproducible—the full archive (preregistration, manifest, responses, provider traces, validator traces, analysis artifacts) and canonical SHA‑256 hashes are released so others can replay, vary generator snapshots, increase task difficulty, use independent initial draws per arm, or permit iterative repairs to probe regimes where automatic repair may matter.

limitations: Single model snapshot (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated — results do not generalize to other models or model versions.

Deterministic validator implements a conservative subset of operational hazards (syntactic checks, interface and workflow invariants) and omits dynamic/emulation‑level checks and deeper routing semantics.

Curated 300‑task manifest may not include adversarial or out‑of‑distribution failure modes; under the chosen prompt and model snapshot every shared initial candidate passed the validator (ceiling effect), limiting the ability to measure G‑V‑R improvements under the preregistered one‑repair policy.

Shared initial‑candidate design (preregistered) fixes the same initial generation for both arms to isolate repair effect; this reduces sensitivity to generator variability and can mask repair value when the generator is already accurate on the task set.
Only a single automatic repair attempt was permitted per task; iterative or human‑in‑the‑loop repair policies were not evaluated.
Automated contamination detection cannot eliminate memorization risk entirely; the preregistered contamination summary reported zero flagged pairs but residual uncertainty remains.
